questions.cardText:
[Anthropology] What is a “fantasy coffin”?
A. A container for valuable items
B. A burial coffin
C. A storage for items from a deceased person
Answer: B. Originating from Ghana, fantasy coffins are elaborately crafted to resemble objects that had significance to the deceased. Examples include coffins shaped like animals, cars, smartphones, or even cigarette boxes.
questions.de: Aus welchem Land stammen „Fantasiesärge“, also Särge in Form von Tieren, Autos und anderen Dingen, die dem Verstorbenen etwas bedeuteten?
questions.en: From which country do “fantasy coffins” come — burial coffins shaped like animals, cars and other objects that mattered to the deceased?

timeline.labelEn: Figurative “fantasy” coffins come into use among Christians in Ghana’s Greater Accra Region
timeline.labelDe: Figurative „Fantasiesärge“ kommen bei Christen in Ghanas Region Greater Accra in Gebrauch

questions.notes: Card correct: functional figurative coffins made in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana, mainly for the Ga people. The card asks what one is; the open question asks the card’s explanation’s other fact, the country of origin.

questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] What is the most abundant element in the universe?
A. Hydrogen B. Oxygen C. Carbon
Answer: A. Despite being the most abundant element in the universe, hydrogen is usually not in its elemental form on Earth because it is so light that it escapes the planet’s gravity unless bound to other elements.
questions.de: Welches ist das häufigste chemische Element im Universum?
questions.en: What is the most abundant chemical element in the universe?

timeline.labelEn: Henry Cavendish identifies hydrogen (“inflammable air”) as a distinct substance
timeline.labelDe: Henry Cavendish erkennt Wasserstoff („brennbare Luft“) als eigenen Stoff

questions.notes: Card correct: about 75% of all baryonic mass (Wikipedia).
